did_you_know.text: Did you know? Azariah son of Oded is mentioned as a prophet upon whom the Spirit of God rested, and he spoke to Asa and to Judah and Benjamin.
Did you know? Azariah’s prophecy presents a clear principle: when Israel seeks the Lord, they find him; and when they abandon him, he abandons them.
Did you know? Azariah describes a time when Israel had no true God, no teaching priest, and no law—a picture of spiritual deprivation and the absence of instructive leadership.
Did you know? According to the prophecy, in times of trouble Israel would return to the Lord and seek him—and find him.
Did you know? During the periods described in the prophecy, there was no peace for travelers or residents, because great turmoil afflicted the inhabitants of the lands.
Did you know? Azariah encouraged Asa and the people to be strong and not give up, promising, “There is a reward for your work.”

Did you know? Following the prophecy, Asa removed the abominations from Judah and Benjamin, as well as from the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim, and he renewed the altar of the Lord in front of the vestibule of the temple.

Did you know? The assembly in Jerusalem took place in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign. It included Judah and Benjamin, as well as people from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had joined him.
Did you know? On the day of the covenant, the people sacrificed seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep from the plunder.
Did you know? Asa removed his mother Maacah from her position because she had made a monstrous image for Asherah. He cut down the image, ground it to powder, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
